skeleton: /Game/Characters/Mannequins/Meshes/SK_Mannequin (89 bones, names/hierarchy/rest pose unchanged from Characters/Dink/HandBindingV2)

MI_Mother_PR_Skin.shading: subsurface profile / skin; SSS.rgb = scatter colour x thickness
MI_Mother_PR_Skin.normal: OpenGL (+Y), flip green for UE as the existing importer does

MI_Mother_PR_Eyes.shading: default lit, low roughness from ORM.G; single-shell eye with modelled cornea bulge

MI_Mother_PR_Hair.shading: hair shading model, MASKED (alpha in BC.a, clip about 0.33 with dithered opacity / TAA), two-sided; cap shell + lock cards + brow and lash cards in one slot
MI_Mother_PR_Hair.anisotropy: FLOW.rg = strand direction in UV space, encoded 0.5 + 0.5 * d (root to tip): world tangent = normalize(d.x * dP/du + d.y * dP/dv); use it as the hair tangent / anisotropy direction so highlights run along the hair. Baked from the strand groom (cap rect) and from the strand clumps (card tiles). N is the strand-relief normal (OpenGL), ORM.r = strand depth occlusion, ORM.g = roughness.
MI_Mother_PR_Hair.masks: FLOW.b = back-light mask (0 on the opaque cap shell, 1 on cards: scale back-scatter / two-sided transmission by it). MSK.r = strand depth, MSK.g = per-strand id (use for per-strand colour / roughness jitter), MSK.b = root-to-tip gradient (0 root, 1 tip; the BC already carries a root-dark to tip-light gradient).
MI_Mother_PR_Hair.atlas_layout: uv: cap texture u 0-0.5, v 0.5-1 (whole groom projected about the head centre, opaque under-fill inside the hairline); 32 narrow lock tiles u 0.5-1, v 0.25-1 (root at top); 4 wide tiles u 0-0.5, v 0.25-0.5; brow groom band u 0-0.5, v 0-0.25; lash band u 0.5-1, v 0-0.25
MI_Mother_PR_Hair.shell_order: vertex attribute hl (also the build order, inner first): 1 = cap shell (opaque, never drop, casts the shadow), 2 = mid lock cards, 3 = outer lock cards, 4 = brows and lashes, 5 = hairline wisps and flyaways. LOD1 keeps all, LOD2 drops 5, LOD3 keeps 1, 3, 4. Custom split normals are scalp-blended and exported in the FBX: import normals, do not recompute.

budget_note: LOD0 about 29.7k triangles: over the 20k soft target, under the 35k hard cap. Head keeps the MakeHuman topology (about 8.6k), hands were thinned to half, hair is about 3k, the dress about 9k.
skirt_check: Tools/check_poke.py, boots against the dress below the knee, shipped walk samples + a turn: 0 boot vertices outside the skirt in idle, 1-23 of about 300 in the walk samples (the trailing heel lifts the back hem and shows below it); before the calf-weighted back hem it was 31-73.
known_weaknesses: Not photoreal at 1 m; passes as a woman in a red dress at gameplay distance. The last review round (r9) still faulted everything below.

Hair cards against the strand groom (Review/r9_hair_compare.png): swept-back shape, parting and colour match at 2 m in sun; faults: the card hair is more even in tone (the strand groom has a thin pale patch and a darker side that the cards lack), pale grey hairs read as bright scratches, on the shadow side the cards break into a dappled pattern with a harder terminator than the strands, and at 0.5 m under overcast the long cards show as overlapping shingles. The bun is a rosette of wound flat ribbons over an opaque core: faceted, with a dark slot at its centre, not the smooth coil of the strand bun. Temple and nape wisps are few and stiff. Lashes are not from a strand groom.

Neckline rebuilt 12 Nov: a smaller round scoop that stays inside the chest skin patch, drawn down onto the skin with a hem lip; the white skin flaps and black gaps are gone (r9_close), but the hem edge is still slightly serrated at 0.6 m and the skin dips about a centimetre under the hem (it is tucked 13 mm so it cannot poke through in motion). The shoulder seams still show a dark slit where the lofted sleeves meet the bodice.

Skin: pore and meso relief and roughness breakup were raised (cfg/skin.json micro, nrm_k, rough_micro, rough_meso); the close-up is less clay-like but now reads slightly orange-peel in raking sun, and wrinkles are still shallow.

Face: built on the shipped middle-aged MakeHuman head with authored age lines, bags and jowls, but it still reads younger than 40-45 and somewhat boyish (round smooth cheeks, large eyes); no expression shapes, no teeth.

Bodice is tight and smooth compared with the skirt; its bust shaping comes from the old dress volume. Sleeves are lofts that pass through the armhole (no modelled seam); the cuff is a plain gathered band.
Build is slimmer than the stout sprite.

Skirt: pleats are authored displacement, not simulated; weights are authored (pelvis / thigh / calf), so a long stride swings the hem wide and the trailing boot shows under the back hem. No cloth simulation or collision in engine is assumed.
Forearms are re-fitted MakeHuman base-mesh faces welded to the hands: plain anatomy, no elbow wrinkles, slightly paler than the face.
Kitchen stains are procedural (grease spots, pale dusting on the lap) and sparse.

No actions embedded; pose tests used the idle boundary pose and four samples of the Epic walk reference plus a hand-made turn. Not imported or seen in Unreal; Physics Asset not made. Validator: whole-mesh UV_OVERLAP error as for Dink (five texture sets); LOD0 over the soft triangle target.
hair: Game hair rebuilt 12 Nov 2026 from the strand groom: (1) an opaque cap shell that carries the whole evaluated groom, projected about the head centre into the cap rect of a 4096 atlas (colour with root-dark to tip-light gradient, strand-relief normal, depth occlusion, flow map; dark under-fill inside the hairline so no scalp shows), (2) narrow lock cards (20-85 hairs per tile, 5-10 mm wide at the tip) laid along the same guide field in two lifted layers that never dip under the cap, (3) hairline wisps and a few flyaways, (4) brow cards baked from a short strand groom. Lashes are still the CC0 MakeHuman lash cards. Acceptance renders: Review/<tag>_hair_compare.png (top = strands, bottom = cards; 2 m sun, 0.5 m sun, 0.5 m overcast, back, crown).
